What meta tags does a modern HTML page need for SEO? Give a full <head> example.
rows.answer:
For SEO, a modern HTML page should include the following meta tags:

- **`<meta name="description" content="Your website description here">`** – This tag provides a concise summary of your site.
- **`<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">`** – Ensures the page is responsive on different devices.
- **`<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=UTF-8">`** – Ensures the page uses UTF-8 for character encoding.

Here's a complete `<head>` example:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>My Website</title>
  <meta name="description" content="Your website description here. This is a modern HTML page for SEO." />
</head>
```

rows.prompt: How does the <picture> element differ from srcset? Show both.
rows.answer:
The `<picture>` element is used to load images from a source URL, while `srcset` is used to specify different image sizes for a given source. Here's how they differ:

### `<picture>`
- **Purpose**: Used to load images from a source URL.
- **Usage**: When you want to use an image from a specific URL, you can include it in the `<picture>` tag.
- **Example**:
```html
<picture>
  <source src="https://example.com/image1.jpg" type="image/png">
  <source src="https://example.com/image2.jpg" type="image/png">
</picture>
```

### `srcset`
- **Purpose**: Used to specify different image sizes for a given source URL.
- **Usage**: When you want to load multiple image sizes from the same source, you can include them in the `srcset` attribute.
- **Example**:
```html
<picture>
  <source src="https://example.com/image1.jpg" type="image/png">
  <source srcset="https://example.com/image2.jpg?size=300x200" type="image/png">
</picture>
```

### Summary:
| Feature | `<picture>` | `srcset` |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Purpose | Load images from a source URL | Specify different image sizes for the same source |

rows.prompt: How do I embed a YouTube video responsively?
rows.answer:
To embed a YouTube video responsively on your website, you can use the `YouTube Video Embed` feature by including the `youtube-iframe` tag in your HTML code. Here's how you can do it:

### Step-by-step:
1. **Include the YouTube Player Script**:
   Add this code to your HTML file where you want to embed a YouTube video:

   ```html
   <iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/your-video-id?enablejsapi=1&estyle=1" width="600" height="450"></iframe>
   ```

2. **Replace `your-video-id`** with the ID of your YouTube video.

### Example:
```html
<iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/your-video-id?enablejsapi=1&estyle=1" width="600" height="450"></iframe>
```

### Explanation:
- The `width` and `height` attributes define the size of the iframe.
- The `enablejsapi=1` and `estyle=1` parameters ensure that the video is embedded correctly.

### Optional:
You can also use YouTube's own embed code if you want to embed videos from their own site, but this method is more flexible for embedding videos from any source.

How do I load Google Fonts correctly?
rows.answer:
To load Google Fonts correctly in your project, you can use the `@font-face` declaration in your HTML file. Here's how you can do it:

### Step-by-step:
1. **Download** the Google Fonts from [https://fonts.google.com/](https://fonts.google.com/)
2. **Locate** the `.ttf` or `.woff` files in your project directory.
3. **Add them to your project's CSS file** (e.g., `style.css`) or include them directly in your HTML.

### Example Code:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Google Fonts</title>
  <style>
    * {
      box-sizing: border-box;
    }

    body {
      font-family: 'Google Fonts', sans-serif;
    }
  </style>
</head>

<body>
  <!-- Your content here -->
</body>

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@fontsource/glyphscript@1.0.0/glyphscript.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@fontsource/googlefonts@1.0.0/GoogleFonts.min.js"></script>
```

### Explanation:
- The `@font-face` declaration in the `<style>` tag loads the Google Fonts from the CDN.
- This ensures that your project uses Google Fonts without needing to download them manually.
